T: Worst team in the world. Best feed after the match.
D: A burnt-out Dutch coach is sent to American Samoa to turn around the worst football team on the planet.
P: Serve the mains when the team finally scores a goal.
S: the loss to Australia nobody forgets

Taro sliced paper thin, fried at 175C until crisp and salted, with a lime and chilli salt. Peel 600g taro and slice paper thin on a mandoline. Fry in batches at 175C for 2 to 3 minutes until crisp and pale golden. Drain and toss with 1 tsp salt mixed with the zest of 1 lime and 1/2 tsp chilli flakes.
raw fish salad, the island way
Fresh white fish cubed and soaked in lime juice, then mixed with coconut cream, cucumber, tomato and onion.
taro leaves baked in coconut cream, a Samoan feast staple

Silverbeet leaves wrapped around onion, garlic and seasoned coconut cream, baked in foil parcels until rich and soft, served with roast taro. Heat the oven to 180C. Peel 800g taro, cut into chunks, toss in oil and salt and roast 45 minutes. Strip the stalks from 1 bunch silverbeet. Mix 400ml coconut cream with 1 finely diced onion, 1 crushed garlic clove and 1 tsp salt. Stack 3 leaves into a cup in your hand, add a few spoons of coconut mix, fold closed and wrap tightly in foil. Make 8 parcels and bake 40 minutes. Open and serve with the taro.
M: Samoan chop suey for the whole squad

Glass noodles stir-fried with chicken, soy, ginger, garlic and vegetables, the dish at every Samoan feast. Soak 250g glass noodles in hot water for 10 minutes and drain. Fry 600g sliced chicken thighs with 3 garlic cloves and a thumb of ginger until browned, then add 2 sliced carrots and 1 onion. Add the noodles, 80ml soy sauce and 250ml water and toss until the noodles soak it all up.
Pisupo corned beef with fried rice
the tinned corned beef that turns up at every Samoan table

Tinned corned beef fried with onion, tomato and cabbage until crispy at the edges, over garlic fried rice with a squeeze of lime and soy. Cook 2 cups rice the day before and chill. Fry 1 sliced onion in oil for 3 minutes, add 2 diced tomatoes and a quarter of a cabbage, shredded, and cook 5 minutes. Break in 340g tinned corned beef and fry over high heat, stirring now and then, until browned in spots. In another pan, fry 3 crushed garlic cloves in oil, add the rice and 2 tbsp soy and toss until hot. Serve the beef over the rice with lime.
W: coconut buns baked in coconut cream
Soft sweet bread rolls baked in a tray of sweetened coconut cream until the sauce turns sticky and golden.
K: Grated Samoan cocoa or dark chocolate melted into hot water and milk with sugar, served hot or poured over ice. Melt 150g dark chocolate into 500ml hot water, then whisk in 500ml milk and 3 tbsp sugar and heat until steaming. Serve hot in mugs, or cool it down and pour over ice for a hot afternoon.

s.note: raw fish salad, the island way
s.how: Cut 400g very fresh white fish fillets into 1cm cubes and cover with the juice of 4 limes. Chill 30 minutes until the fish turns white. Drain most of the juice, then stir in 200ml coconut cream, 1 diced cucumber, 2 diced tomatoes and half a finely diced red onion. Season and serve cold.

w.note: coconut buns baked in coconut cream
w.how: Mix 500g flour, 7g dried yeast, 50g sugar, 50g soft butter and 300ml warm water into a dough and prove 1 hour. Shape 12 buns into a baking dish. Mix 400ml coconut cream with 100g sugar, pour over and bake at 180C for 30 minutes until golden and sticky.

d.how: Melt 150g dark chocolate into 500ml hot water, then whisk in 500ml milk and 3 tbsp sugar and heat until steaming. Serve hot in mugs, or cool it down and pour over ice for a hot afternoon.
